card: Fixes security logic in contrib/verify-binaries/verify.py where untrusted signatures in a user's GPG keyring were erroneously added to the trusted signature count. It ensures only distinct, non-revoked keys matching trusted fingerprints satisfy the minimum signature requirement, matching full fingerprints from GnuPG VALIDSIG status lines and deduplicating by primary key. Without this fix, users verifying release binaries could accept binaries signed only by untrusted keys present in their local keyring. Includes unit tests for the verification script.
evidence: PR description: 'verify_shasums_signature previously separated signatures into good_trusted and good_untrusted, but computed num_trusted = len(good_trusted) + len(good_untrusted). As a result, 3 valid signatures from untrusted keys present in the local GPG keyring satisfied --min-good-sigs even when none of them were trusted in GPG or matched --trusted-keys.'

Commit 5fddfefe64: 'Count only distinct non-revoked trusted signers toward the threshold, match --trusted-keys against full fingerprints from GNUPG VALIDSIG status lines while deduplicating by primary key fingerprint across active and expired signatures, and add unit tests in contrib/verify-binaries/test.py.'
problem: `verify_shasums_signature` calculated trusted signatures as `len(good_trusted) + len(good_untrusted)`, allowing valid signatures from untrusted keys in a user's local keyring to satisfy `--min-good-sigs` without matching `--trusted-keys`. Furthermore, `parse_gpg_result` only read key IDs from `GOODSIG` instead of full fingerprints from `VALIDSIG`, counted revoked keys (`REVKEYSIG`), and did not deduplicate multiple signatures from the same primary key.

risk.why: A bug in this script could falsely pass or fail binary signature verification for users running contrib/verify-binaries/verify.py.

scope_notes: Touches release verification scripts and adds unit test cases in contrib/verify-binaries.
summary: Fixes signature verification in `contrib/verify-binaries/verify.py` so that only distinct, non-revoked signatures from trusted keys count toward the minimum signature threshold. It extracts full primary key fingerprints from GnuPG `VALIDSIG` lines to properly match `--trusted-keys` and deduplicate signers, and adds unit test coverage.
